name_translation: The Yoga of Knowledge and Realization

verses.text_sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच |
मय्यासक्तमनाः पार्थ योगं युञ्जन्मदाश्रयः |
असंशयं समग्रं मां यथा ज्ञास्यसि तच्छृणु || १ ||
verses.transliteration:
śrībhagavānuvāca |
mayyāsaktamanāḥ pārtha yogaṃ yuñjanmadāśrayaḥ |
asaṃśayaṃ samagraṃ māṃ yathā jñāsyasi tacchṛṇu || 1 ||
verses.translation: The Supreme Lord said: Hear, O Partha, how with your mind firmly attached to Me, practicing Yoga with your refuge in Me alone, you shall know Me completely and without any doubt.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna initiates the central mystical teachings of the Gita. Moving from self-discipline and meditation in Chapter 6 to experiential God-realization, the Lord reveals that supreme wisdom unfolds naturally when one takes total refuge in the Divine with unwavering love.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ज्ञानं तेऽहं सविज्ञानमिदं वक्ष्याम्यशेषतः |
यज्ज्ञात्वा नेह भूयोऽन्यज्ज्ञातव्यमवशिष्यते || २ ||
verses.transliteration:
jñānaṃ te'haṃ savijñānamidaṃ vakṣyāmyaśeṣataḥ |
yajjñātvā neha bhūyo'nyajjñātavyamavaśiṣyate || 2 ||
verses.translation: I shall declare to you in full this theoretical knowledge (Jnana) combined with direct experiential realization (Vijnana), knowing which nothing further remains to be known in this world.
verses.meaning: Jnana is intellectual comprehension of the Divine truth through scriptures, whereas Vijnana is personal, living experiential absorption in that truth. Realizing God in totality fulfills the ultimate quest of human consciousness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
मनुष्याणां सहस्रेषु कश्चिद्यतति सिद्धये |
यततामपि सिद्धानां कश्चिन्मां वेत्ति तत्त्वतः || ३ ||
verses.transliteration:
manuṣyāṇāṃ sahasreṣu kaścidyatati siddhaye |
yatatāmapi siddhānāṃ kaścinmāṃ vetti tattvataḥ || 3 ||
verses.translation: Among thousands of human beings, scarcely one strives for spiritual perfection; and among those who strive and achieve success, scarcely one knows Me in truth and essence.
verses.meaning: Human life is commonly distracted by material pursuits. Few feel the burning thirst for liberation, and among dedicated seekers, only a rare, devoted soul transcends all conceptual illusions to perceive the Supreme Reality in His eternal divine personality.

verses.text_sanskrit:
भूमिरापोऽनलो वायुः खं मनो बुद्धिरेव च |
अहङ्कार इतीयं मे भिन्ना प्रकृतिरष्टधा || ४ ||
verses.transliteration:
bhūmirāpo'nalo vāyuḥ khaṃ mano buddhireva ca |
ahaṅkāra itīyaṃ me bhinnā prakṛtiraṣṭadhā || 4 ||
verses.translation: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, intellect, and ego—these constitute My eightfold separated material nature (Apara Prakriti).
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna delineates the cosmic mechanics of the manifest universe. The five gross elements together with the subtle instruments of perception—Manas (mind), Buddhi (discriminating intellect), and Ahankara (individuated ego)—comprise the Lord's insentient, material energy.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अपरेयमितस्त्वन्यां प्रकृतिं विद्धि मे पराम् |
जीवभूतां महाबाहो ययेदं धार्यते जगत् || ५ ||
verses.transliteration:
apareyamitastvanyāṃ prakṛtiṃ viddhi me parām |
jīvabhūtāṃ mahābāho yayedaṃ dhāryate jagat || 5 ||
verses.translation: Besides this inferior material nature, O mighty-armed Arjuna, know My superior spiritual energy (Para Prakriti), which comprises the living beings (Jivas) by whom this universe is sustained.
verses.meaning: Transcending the inanimate physical cosmos is the Lord's higher, conscious spiritual nature—the Jiva-shakti (individual conscious souls). This indwelling consciousness animates, upholds, and interacts with matter, deriving its life directly from the Supreme Lord.

verses.text_sanskrit:
एतद्योनीनि भूतानि सर्वाणीत्युपधारय |
अहं कृत्स्नस्य जगतः प्रभवः प्रलयस्तथा || ६ ||
verses.transliteration:
etadyonīni bhūtāni sarvāṇītyupadhāraya |
ahaṃ kṛtsnasya jagataḥ prabhavaḥ pralayastathā || 6 ||
verses.translation: Know that all created beings have their source of birth in these two natures. I am the sole origin and also the final dissolution of the entire cosmic manifestation.
verses.meaning: All life and cosmic phenomena emerge from the union of Krishna's conscious and material energies. The Supreme Lord is both the efficient cause and the material womb of the universe; everything originates from Him, abides in Him, and dissolves back into Him.

verses.text_sanskrit:
मत्तः परतरं नान्यत्किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय |
मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव || ७ ||
verses.transliteration:
mattaḥ parataraṃ nānyatkiñcidasti dhanañjaya |
mayi sarvamidaṃ protaṃ sūtre maṇigaṇā iva || 7 ||
verses.translation: There is nothing whatsoever higher than Me, O Conqueror of Wealth (Arjuna). All this universe is strung upon Me like clusters of precious gems upon a golden thread.
verses.meaning: One of the most poetic and celebrated verses of the Gita. Sri Krishna reveals His absolute supremacy and omnipresence: just as a hidden golden string holds diverse pearls into a harmonious necklace, the unmanifest Supreme Spirit sustains and unifies the infinite diversity of creation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
रसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय प्रभास्मि शशिसूर्ययोः |
प्रणवः सर्ववेदेषु शब्दः खे पौरुषं नृषु || ८ ||
verses.transliteration:
raso'hamapsu kaunteya prabhāsmi śaśisūryayoḥ |
praṇavaḥ sarvavedeṣu śabdaḥ khe pauruṣaṃ nṛṣu || 8 ||
verses.translation: I am the essential taste in water, O son of Kunti; I am the radiant splendor in the moon and the sun; I am the sacred syllable OM (Pranava) in all the Vedas, the sound in ether, and the noble virility in humanity.
verses.meaning: The Lord is the essential defining principle and vitalizing core of every phenomenon. He is the thirst-quenching essence of water, the luminosity of celestial bodies, the cosmic vibration OM of Vedic revelation, and the inherent potential in humankind.

verses.text_sanskrit:
पुण्यो गन्धः पृथिव्यां च तेजश्चास्मि विभावसौ |
जीवनं सर्वभूतेषु तपश्चास्मि तपस्विषु || ९ ||
verses.transliteration:
puṇyo gandhaḥ pṛthivyāṃ ca tejaścāsmi vibhāvasau |
jīvanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu tapaścāsmi tapasviṣu || 9 ||
verses.translation: I am the sweet and sacred fragrance of the earth, and the brilliant radiance in fire. I am the life-force in all living beings, and the spiritual austerity in ascetic seekers.
verses.meaning: Every purity and potency in nature is a direct expression of Krishna's divine presence. The primal aroma of parched earth kissed by rain, the brilliance of sacrificial flames, the breath of life sustaining creatures, and the focused discipline of yogis are all manifestations of the Lord.

verses.text_sanskrit:
बीजं मां सर्वभूतानां विद्धि पार्थ सनातनम् |
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् || १० ||
verses.transliteration:
bījaṃ māṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ viddhi pārtha sanātanam |
buddhirbuddhimatāmasmi tejastejasvināmaham || 10 ||
verses.translation: Know Me, O Partha, to be the eternal, primeval seed of all entities. I am the sharp intellect of the wise, and the majestic glory of the valiant.
verses.meaning: Krishna is the imperishable root cause from which all species and cosmic cycles germinate. He is the penetrating insight in intellectuals and the spiritual brilliance in great leaders.

verses.text_sanskrit:
बलं बलवतां चाहं कामरागविवर्जितम् |
धर्माविरुद्धो भूतेषु कामोऽस्मि भरतर्षभ || ११ ||
verses.transliteration:
balaṃ balavatāṃ cāhaṃ kāmarāgavivarjitam |
dharmāviruddho bhūteṣu kāmo'smi bharatarṣabha || 11 ||
verses.translation: I am the strength of the mighty that is untainted by selfish lust and craving; and in all beings, O best of the Bharatas, I am desire that is strictly in harmony with Dharma (righteousness).
verses.meaning: Strength exercised for protection and justice without egoic passion is divine. Moreover, desire is not inherently evil when it aligns with cosmic moral law (Dharma)—such as the noble aspiration for truth, duty, and righteous family lineage.

verses.text_sanskrit:
ये चैव सात्त्विका भावा राजसास्तामसाश्च ये |
मत्त एवेति तान्विद्धि न त्वहं तेषु ते मयि || १२ ||
verses.transliteration:
ye caiva sāttvikā bhāvā rājasāstāmasāśca ye |
matta eveti tānviddhi na tvahaṃ teṣu te mayi || 12 ||
verses.translation: Know that whatever states of being there are—whether of Sattva (goodness), Rajas (passion), or Tamas (ignorance)—all emanate from Me alone. Yet I am not bound by them; they are in Me, but I am not in them.
verses.meaning: The three modes of material nature (Gunas) derive their existence from the Lord's power, yet the Supreme Lord remains eternally transcendental, unattached, and unaffected by the modes of Prakriti.

verses.text_sanskrit:
त्रिभिर्गुणमयैर्भावैरेभिः सर्वमिदं जगत् |
मोहितं नाभिजानाति मामेभ्यः परमव्ययम् || १३ ||
verses.transliteration:
tribhirguṇamayairbhāvairebhiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat |
mohitaṃ nābhijānāti māmebhyaḥ paramavyayam || 13 ||
verses.translation: Deluded by these three modes of nature (Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas), this entire world fails to recognize Me, who am situated supreme above the gunas and imperishable.
verses.meaning: Humanity is captivated and enchanted by the shifting play of nature's three colors—serenity, ambition, and lethargy. Blinded by this cosmic veil, embodied souls fail to discern the timeless, immutable Lord standing behind the stage.

verses.text_sanskrit:
दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया दुरत्यया |
मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते || १४ ||
verses.transliteration:
daivī hyeṣā guṇamayī mama māyā duratyayā |
māmeva ye prapadyante māyāmetāṃ taranti te || 14 ||
verses.translation: For this divine, wondrous illusory energy of Mine (Maya), consisting of the three gunas, is extremely difficult to overcome. But those who surrender unto Me alone easily cross beyond this ocean of illusion.
verses.meaning: One of the cardinal verses of Hindu metaphysics. Maya is not an independent power but the divine potency of God Himself; therefore, human ego and intellectual analysis alone cannot dismantle it. Only through sincere loving surrender (Sharanagati) to Sri Krishna does the illusion dissolve like mist before the rising sun.

verses.text_sanskrit:
न मां दुष्कृतिनो मूढाः प्रपद्यन्ते नराधमाः |
माययापहृतज्ञाना आसुरं भावमाश्रिताः || १५ ||
verses.transliteration:
na māṃ duṣkṛtino mūḍhāḥ prapadyante narādhamāḥ |
māyayāpahṛtajñānā āsuraṃ bhāvamāśritāḥ || 15 ||
verses.translation: The wicked, the foolish, and the lowest among men do not surrender unto Me. Their discriminating wisdom is stolen away by Maya, and they embrace a demonic, materialistic nature.
verses.meaning: Those consumed by egoism, arrogance, and unethical conduct remain trapped in spiritual blindness. Having surrendered their intellect to sensory desires and atheistic worldviews, they reject divine refuge and perpetuate suffering.

verses.text_sanskrit:
चतुर्विधा भजन्ते मां जनाः सुकृतिनोऽर्जुन |
आर्तो जिज्ञासुरर्थार्थी ज्ञानी च भरतर्षभ || १६ ||
verses.transliteration:
caturvidhā bhajante māṃ janāḥ sukṛtino'rjuna |
ārto jijñāsurarthārthī jñānī ca bharatarṣabha || 16 ||
verses.translation: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, O Arjuna: the distressed (Arta), the seeker of truth (Jijnasu), the seeker of material prosperity (Artharthi), and the person of spiritual wisdom (Jnani), O best of the Bharatas.
verses.meaning: Krishna graciously classifies the virtuous devotees who turn to Him: those in physical or emotional crisis seeking relief, those driven by philosophical curiosity to understand truth, those praying for material security, and the enlightened sage whose heart is bathed in pure love of God.

verses.text_sanskrit:
तेषां ज्ञानी नित्ययुक्त एकभक्तिर्विशिष्यते |
प्रियो हि ज्ञानिनोऽत्यर्थमहं स च मम प्रियः || १७ ||
verses.transliteration:
teṣāṃ jñānī nityayukta ekabhaktirviśiṣyate |
priyo hi jñānino'tyarthamahaṃ sa ca mama priyaḥ || 17 ||
verses.translation: Of these, the person of wisdom (Jnani), who is constantly steadfast and endowed with one-pointed devotion, is the foremost. For I am exceedingly dear to the wise devotee, and they are exceedingly dear to Me.
verses.meaning: While all devotees are noble, the Jnani bhakta stands supreme because their devotion is unconditional and selfless. They seek neither boons nor escape from distress, but seek God solely for the sake of God. This pure alignment creates an unbreakable bond of reciprocal divine love.

verses.text_sanskrit:
उदाराः सर्व एवैते ज्ञानी त्वात्मैव मे मतम् |
आस्थितः स हि युक्तात्मा मामेवानुत्तमां गतिम् || १८ ||
verses.transliteration:
udārāḥ sarva evaite jñānī tvātmaiva me matam |
āsthitaḥ sa hi yuktātmā māmevānuttamāṃ gatim || 18 ||
verses.translation: Noble indeed are all these devotees, but I consider the person of wisdom to be My very own Self (Atman). For with a mind harmonized in Yoga, they are firmly established in Me as the supreme destination.
verses.meaning: Sri Krishna magnificently honors every sincere seeker as noble (Udara), showing divine magnanimity. Yet He regards the Jnani as non-different from His own Self, because the sage has merged their identity into the supreme consciousness.

verses.text_sanskrit:
बहूनां जन्मनामन्ते ज्ञानवान्मां प्रपद्यते |
वासुदेवः सर्वमिति स महात्मा सुदुर्लभः || १९ ||
verses.transliteration:
bahūnāṃ janmanāmante jñānavānmāṃ prapadyate |
vāsudevaḥ sarvamiti sa mahātmā sudurlabhaḥ || 19 ||
verses.translation: After countless lifetimes of spiritual evolution, the person of true wisdom surrenders unto Me, realizing that 'Vasudeva (Lord Krishna) is everything.' Such a great soul (Mahatma) is exceedingly rare.
verses.meaning: The pinnacle of Vedantic realization: The enlightened soul does not see God as distant or separate, but beholds the omnipresent Vasudeva vibrating in every atom, person, mountain, and star. Such cosmic devotional vision is the rare fruit of lifetimes of spiritual maturity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
कामैस्तैस्तैर्हृतज्ञानाः प्रपद्यन्तेऽन्यदेवताः |
तं तं नियममास्थाय प्रकृत्या नियताः स्वया || २० ||
verses.transliteration:
kāmaistaistairhṛtajñānāḥ prapadyante'nyadevatāḥ |
taṃ taṃ niyamamāsthāya prakṛtyā niyatāḥ svayā || 20 ||
verses.translation: Those whose spiritual discrimination has been stolen away by various selfish desires surrender unto other deities (Devatas), observing specific rituals and vows according to their own conditioned natures.
verses.meaning: When human beings are consumed by cravings for temporal wealth, fame, or celestial pleasures, they worship secondary demigods for quick material boons rather than seeking eternal union with the Supreme Lord.

verses.text_sanskrit:
यो यो यां यां तनुं भक्तः श्रद्धयार्चितुमिच्छति |
तस्य तस्याचलां श्रद्धां तामेव विदधाम्यहम् || २१ ||
verses.transliteration:
yo yo yāṃ yāṃ tanuṃ bhaktaḥ śraddhayārcitumicchati |
tasya tasyācalāṃ śraddhāṃ tāmeva vidadhāmyaham || 21 ||
verses.translation: Whatever celestial form a devotee desires to worship with sincere faith, I alone make that faith steady and unwavering.
verses.meaning: A profound testament to the inclusive compassion of the Hindu worldview. The Supreme Lord does not condemn sincere faith in different forms; rather, He Himself indwells the devotee's heart to empower and steady their faith, guiding them upward along their evolutionary path.

verses.text_sanskrit:
स तया श्रद्धया युक्तस्तस्याराधनमीहते |
लभते च ततः कामान्मयैव विहितान्हि तान् || २२ ||
verses.transliteration:
sa tayā śraddhayā yuktastasyārādhanamīhate |
labhate ca tataḥ kāmānmayaiva vihitānhi tān || 22 ||
verses.translation: Endowed with that faith, such a devotee performs the worship of that deity and obtains their desired benefits; but in truth, those rewards are ordained by Me alone.
verses.meaning: Demigods possess no independent power to grant boons; all cosmic forces operate by the grace and laws of the Supreme Lord. The fruits received through any channel ultimately flow from Krishna's divine dispensation.

verses.text_sanskrit:
अन्तवत्तु फलं तेषां तद्भवत्यल्पमेधसाम् |
देवान्देवयजो यान्ति मद्भक्ता यान्ति मामपि || २३ ||
verses.transliteration:
antavattu phalaṃ teṣāṃ tadbhavatyalpamedhasām |
devāndevayajo yānti madbhaktā yānti māmapi || 23 ||
verses.translation: Finite and perishable is the fruit gained by people of small intelligence. The worshippers of celestial gods go to the heavenly realms, but My devotees come directly unto Me.
verses.meaning: Temporal desires yield only transient celestial pleasures that exhaust when karma runs out. In contrast, those who dedicate their devotion to the Supreme Lord attain the timeless, imperishable realm of eternal bliss (Moksha).

verses.text_sanskrit:
अव्यक्तं व्यक्तिमापन्नं मन्यन्ते मामबुद्धयः |
परं भावमजानन्तो ममाव्ययमनुत्तमम् || २४ ||
verses.transliteration:
avyaktaṃ vyaktimāpannaṃ manyante māmabuddhayaḥ |
paraṃ bhāvamajānanto mamāvyayamanuttamam || 24 ||
verses.translation: The unenlightened, unaware of My supreme, imperishable, and unsurpassable nature, think of Me as an unmanifest spirit that has merely acquired a mortal physical form.
verses.meaning: Those lacking spiritual depth fail to recognize Krishna's divine descent (Avatara). They mistake the Lord for an ordinary human who became divine or a formless entity limited by mortal flesh, failing to see His transcendental, omnipotent divinity.

verses.text_sanskrit:
नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः |
मूढोऽयं नाभिजानाति लोको मामजमव्ययम् || २५ ||
verses.transliteration:
nāhaṃ prakāśaḥ sarvasya yogamāyāsamāvṛtaḥ |
mūḍho'yaṃ nābhijānāti loko māmajamavyayam || 25 ||
verses.translation: I am not manifest to all, being veiled by My divine illusory energy (Yoga Maya). This deluded world fails to recognize Me, who am unborn and imperishable.
verses.meaning: Yoga Maya acts as a cosmic curtain. While the Lord is everywhere, worldly eyes blinded by material desire see only the external world. His divine glory reveals itself solely to the pure-hearted devotee.

verses.text_sanskrit:
वेदाहं समतीतानि वर्तमानानि चार्जुन |
भविष्याणि च भूतानि मां तु वेद न कश्चन || २६ ||
verses.transliteration:
vedāhaṃ samatītāni vartamānāni cārjuna |
bhaviṣyāṇi ca bhūtāni māṃ tu veda na kaścana || 26 ||
verses.translation: I know all beings of the past, the present, and the future, O Arjuna; but Me no one knows in totality.
verses.meaning: As the timeless, omniscient Lord of Cosmic Consciousness, Sri Krishna has complete knowledge of all beings across all dimensions of time, while mortal intellects, bound by time and space, cannot comprehend the infinite.

verses.text_sanskrit:
इच्छाद्वेषसमुत्थेन द्वन्द्वमोहेन भारत |
सर्वभूतानि सम्मोहं सर्गे यान्ति परन्तप || २७ ||
verses.transliteration:
icchādveṣasamutthena dvandvamohena bhārata |
sarvabhūtāni sammohaṃ sarge yānti parantapa || 27 ||
verses.translation: By the delusion of dualities arising from attraction and repulsion (desire and hatred), O descendant of Bharata, all living beings fall into deep delusion at the time of birth, O scorcher of foes.
verses.meaning: From the moment embodied souls take birth, the psychological oscillation between liking (Raga) and disliking (Dvesha) creates the illusion of duality, keeping consciousness trapped in worldly confusion.

verses.text_sanskrit:
येषां त्वन्तगतं पापं जनानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् |
ते द्वन्द्वमोहनिर्मुक्ता भजन्ते मां दृढव्रताः || २८ ||
verses.transliteration:
yeṣāṃ tvantagataṃ pāpaṃ janānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām |
te dvandvamohanirmuktā bhajante māṃ dṛḍhavratāḥ || 28 ||
verses.translation: But those virtuous persons whose sins have come to an end through righteous deeds are liberated from the delusion of dualities; they worship Me with steadfast determination and unwavering vows.
verses.meaning: Selfless service and righteous living cleanse the subconscious mind of past negative impressions (Samskaras). Freed from the swings of pleasure and pain, the purified soul worships the Lord with resolute spiritual determination.

verses.text_sanskrit:
जरामरणमोक्षाय मामाश्रित्य यतन्ति ये |
ते ब्रह्म तद्विदुः कृत्स्नमध्यात्मं कर्म चाखिलम् || २९ ||
verses.transliteration:
jarāmaraṇamokṣāya māmāśritya yatanti ye |
te brahma tadviduḥ kṛtsnamadhyātmaṃ karma cākhilam || 29 ||
verses.translation: Those who take refuge in Me and strive for liberation from old age and death come to know that Supreme Brahman in full, the inner Self (Adhyatma), and the complete truth of action (Karma).
verses.meaning: Devotees seeking freedom from the cycle of birth and mortality through total surrender to Sri Krishna receive holistic spiritual enlightenment: they realize the unmanifest Absolute (Brahman), the indwelling Self (Adhyatma), and the mystery of cosmic action (Karma).

verses.text_sanskrit:
साधिभूताधिदैवं मां साधियज्ञं च ये विदुः |
प्रयाणकालेऽपि च मां ते विदुर्युक्तचेतसः || ३० ||
verses.transliteration:
sādhibhūtādhidaivaṃ māṃ sādhiyajñaṃ ca ye viduḥ |
prayāṇakāle'pi ca māṃ te viduryuktacetasaḥ || 30 ||
verses.translation: Those who know Me as the governing principle of the material realm (Adhibhuta), the divine realm (Adhidaiva), and the realm of sacrifice (Adhiyajna)—they, with their minds steadfastly merged in Me, know Me even at the critical moment of death.
verses.meaning: The grand concluding verse of Chapter 7 sets the theological foundation for Chapter 8. The enlightened devotee sees Sri Krishna as the sole reality governing nature, gods, and sacred sacrifice. Such integrated awareness remains unbroken even during physical departure, leading directly to eternal liberation.
